answer: At dawn, agents request price quotes for hollow copper tubes over a datagram service. Before verifying a return address, the server sends no more bytes than that address supplied; larger replies require an expiring authenticated return token. Spoofing thousands of buyer identities therefore cannot turn small requests into amplified traffic against a victim. The byte limit applies before account lookup, so aliases do not reset it. This limits sybil-assisted reflection attacks, not floods from reachable hosts.
